title: Transported fixed-pair functors and common derived resolution models
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] in compatible chosen universes, with additive autoequivalences $F,H$. Write $\mathcal B=\mathcal C^F$, $\mathcal E=\mathcal D^H$ and $U_F,U_H$ for the fixed-pair categories and forgetting [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Assume $\mathcal B,\mathcal E$ are Grothendieck abelian, that $U_F,U_H$ create finite limits and are exact and conservative, and that $U_F$ preserves K-injective complexes. Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and left exact, and $e:HL\xrightarrow{\sim}LF$ natural. The formulas
$$\widetilde L(X,\theta)=(LX,L(\theta)\circ e_X),\qquad\widetilde L(a)=L(a)$$
define an additive left exact functor $\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$, with $U_H\widetilde L=LU_F$ on objects, morphisms, complexes and homotopies. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and total right derived functors with units [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For every complex $K$ in $\mathcal B$ there is a K-injective resolution $s:K\to I$; every such resolution has $U_Fs$ a K-injective resolution of $U_FK$. There are canonical resolution isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal D)$
$$D(U_H)R\widetilde L(Q_{\mathcal B}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal D}U_H\widetilde L(I)=Q_{\mathcal D}L(U_FI)\xleftarrow{\sim}RL(D(U_F)Q_{\mathcal B}K).$$
Thus the two derived values have a specified common complex model, giving an objectwise comparison by the identity on that model. For a chain map $t:I\to I'$ of K-injective complexes of $\mathcal B$, the two derived computations send $Qt$ to the same map $Q_{\mathcal D}L(U_Ft)$ under these isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Put $\alpha_X=L(\theta_X)e_X:HLX\to LX$. It is an isomorphism, with inverse $e_X^{-1}L(\theta_X^{-1})$. If $a:(X,\theta_X)\to(Y,\theta_Y)$ is a fixed-pair morphism [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], then naturality of $e$ gives
$$L(a)\alpha_X=L(a\theta_X)e_X=L(\theta_Y F(a))e_X=L(\theta_Y)e_YHL(a)=\alpha_YHL(a).$$
Thus $L(a)$ is a morphism of the proposed target pairs. The identity and composition laws follow from those of $L$. This constructs $\widetilde L$ and gives $U_H\widetilde L=LU_F$ on objects and morphisms.

Addition and zero of fixed-pair morphisms are their underlying addition and zero: the commuting equation is closed under addition because $F,H$ are additive [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Therefore $\widetilde L(a+b)=L(a+b)=L(a)+L(b)$, and both forgetful functors are additive. For a finite diagram $T$ in $\mathcal B$ with limit $P$, the underlying cone $U_FP\to U_FT$ is limiting since $U_F$ creates finite limits. Applying the left exact $L$ leaves a limiting cone. Its legs are exactly those of $\widetilde LP\to\widetilde LT$ after $U_H$. This cone is limiting in $\mathcal E$: the unique underlying mediating map is a fixed-pair morphism, since its commuting equation holds after every limit projection (the legs already commute with the structure maps), and the projections are jointly monic. Its uniqueness follows from faithfulness of forgetting. This also treats the empty diagram. Hence $\widetilde L$ is left exact.

proof.text: Apply these functors degreewise to complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both composites have terms $L(U_FK^r)$ and differentials $L(U_Fd^r)$, and on chain maps both have components $L(U_Fa^r)$. A chain homotopy $h$ is sent by both to the same components $L(U_Fh^r)$: additivity carries $a-b=dh+hd$ to the corresponding equation. Thus the equality of step 1 holds on complexes and homotopies. Termwise additive functors commute with shifts and mapping cones: the shifted differential $-d$ maps to $-L(d)$ and the cone matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d'&a\\0&-d\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ maps to the same matrix with $L$ applied to every entry, using its canonical biproduct identification. Consequently their functors from the homotopy categories to the target derived categories are exact.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] to the assumed Grothendieck abelian categories $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C$. Every complex of each has a K-injective resolution; in particular choose $s:K\to I$ in $\mathcal B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], the exact additive $U_F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so $U_Fs$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its target $U_FI$ is K-injective by the assumed preservation of K-injectives by $U_F$. This proves the assertion for every such $s$, not just the chosen replacement functor. Step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] give the total right derived functors of $\widetilde L$ and $L$, with units $\widetilde\eta,\eta$ and isomorphic unit components at K-injectives as specified by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor].

Use the natural localization identification $\varphi_J:D(U_H)Q_{\mathcal E}J\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal D}U_HJ$ of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For the resolution $s:K\to I$ define
$$a_s=\varphi_{\widetilde LI}\,D(U_H)(\widetilde\eta_I^{-1})\,D(U_H)(R\widetilde L(Q_{\mathcal B}s)),\qquad b_s=\eta_{U_FI}^{-1}\,RL(Q_{\mathcal C}U_Fs).$$
Composition here is read right to left. Both are isomorphisms: the localized resolutions are invertible, and the two unit components are invertible on the K-injectives of step 4 [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The source of $a_s$ is $D(U_H)R\widetilde L(Q_{\mathcal B}K)$; the source of $b_s$ is $RL(Q_{\mathcal C}U_FK)$, identified with $RL(D(U_F)Q_{\mathcal B}K)$ by the same exact-functor factorization for $U_F$. Their targets are respectively $Q_{\mathcal D}U_H\widetilde LI$ and $Q_{\mathcal D}L(U_FI)$, which are the identical complex model by step 3. These are the claimed canonical resolution isomorphisms. In particular $b_s^{-1}a_s$ is the comparison obtained by the identity on that model.

proof.text:
For a chain map $t:I\to I'$ between K-injectives, use the identity resolutions of $I,I'$ in step 5. Naturality of the unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] reads
$$R\widetilde L(Q_{\mathcal B}t)\,\widetilde\eta_I=\widetilde\eta_{I'}\,Q_{\mathcal E}(\widetilde Lt).$$
Conjugate by the two invertible unit components, apply $D(U_H)$, and use naturality of $\varphi$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. This yields
$$a_{1_{I'}}D(U_H)R\widetilde L(Q_{\mathcal B}t)a_{1_I}^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal D}U_H\widetilde L(t)=Q_{\mathcal D}L(U_Ft).$$
The same unit-naturality equation for $L$ at $U_Ft$ gives
$$b_{1_{I'}}RL(Q_{\mathcal C}U_Ft)b_{1_I}^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal D}L(U_Ft).$$
The exact-functor factorization identifies the middle map on the left with $RL(D(U_F)(Q_{\mathcal B}t))$. These equalities prove the last clause, including equality of the actual maps on the common model.
